analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Risk appetite was positive at the start of the week. The S&P 500 gained 0.70%, the Nasdaq Composite 0.82% and the STOXX 600 0.77%, and longer-dated bonds mostly rallied. US and European futures are slightly lower this morning (S&P 500 -0.09%, Nasdaq -0.38%, Stoxx -0.41%).

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.82% after falling 3.21% last week, and the Mag 7 gained 0.76%. CoreWeave rose 1.76% even though it fell pre-market after Elon Musk wrote on X on Sunday that neoclouds would see 'guppy-level death and consolidation', because debt markets would be reluctant to finance companies that depend on AI data centres for their revenues.

Single-stock moves: Meta fell 1.88% after announcing plans to raise as much as $95bn through a stock sale. Microsoft rose 1.54% after saying it will offer buyouts to about 60,000 employees to cut costs.

France was the main story in European rates. Moody's left France's credit rating unchanged on Friday and the weekend protests were controlled. The 10yr OAT yield fell 11.6bps and the OAT-Bund spread tightened 13.8bps to 153bps, the largest one-day narrowing since March 2020. A 2.2bp rise in the 10yr Bund yield amplified the move. The 10yr BTP yield fell 8.2bps and the gilt yield fell 1.2bps.

The 2yr Bund yield rose 4.9bps, while 2yr French yields fell 4.5bps and 2yr Italian yields fell 2.5bps. DB attributes the Bund move to some unwinding of flight to quality, an energy component and a stronger-than-expected German IFO survey. The IFO expectations component rose to 91.6 against 90.0 expected, its highest since 2022.

In the US, the 2yr Treasury yield rose 3.5bps, reversing some of last week's decline in the risk-on tone. Longer maturities rallied as US energy prices pulled back. The 10yr yield is 2.1bps lower at 4.968% as of this morning.

Brazilian assets sold off sharply after President Lula's surprise election victory over Flávio Bolsonaro. The Bovespa fell 13.88% and the real fell 8.06%, the worst USD-adjusted day for domestic equities in nearly 35 years, though not as bad as the same time the previous day.

Oil stayed volatile. Brent settled 0.78% lower at $115.81/bbl and WTI 1.46% lower at $101.76/bbl, after news of talks between Iran and the Mecca Pact countries. Brent touched $117.44/bbl intraday on a Reuters report that Hezbollah was preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities with Israel. It is down another 1.04% this morning.
European natural gas futures rose 3.01% to a post-2022 high of €96.68/MWh on a supply outage in Norway, while US natural gas fell 1.44% to a 6-month low on warm weather.

Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan (the Mecca Defence Alliance) met Iranian representatives in Tehran to promote regional stability. Iranian state media said Iran would support 'any understanding' that strengthened regional unity. The overall market move was muted because investors are wary of extrapolating from diplomacy, and last week there were reports that US and Israeli militaries had begun drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran.

Israel holds an election today. Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot has a clear route to the 61 Knesset seats needed. DB economists see outcomes ranging from another Netanyahu-led government to an opposition or unity government, deadlock or another election. Both sides agree on preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon. Eisenkot would intervene militarily if necessary but stop short of regime change, while Netanyahu says regime change is ultimately necessary. The difference could matter if tensions re-escalate after the US midterms.

Asia is mostly higher this morning. The KOSPI is up 3.27%, led by Samsung Electronics (+4.23%) and SK Hynix (+6.12%), helped by South Korean Q3 GDP of +3.4% y/y against +3.0% expected. The Nikkei is up 1.55% and the ASX 200 up 0.49%. Chinese equities lag, with the CSI 300 down 0.39%, the Hang Seng down 0.64% and the Shanghai Composite down 0.45%.

Chinese industrial profits rose 14.4% y/y in September, the fastest growth since June, driven by AI-related industries, while consumer-facing sectors face weak domestic demand. Profits for the first nine months of 2026 rose 15.5%, slightly below the 15.7% for January-August.

Today's calendar: US October Conference Board consumer confidence, Richmond Fed indices, September durable goods orders and new home sales. Europe has French consumer confidence and Eurozone M3. Earnings include Visa, HSBC, NXP Semiconductors, Teradyne and Boeing. The US Treasury auctions $70bn of 5yr notes. The FOMC and major tech earnings are the focus later in the week.

risk_factors: Re-escalation between the US/Israel and Iran, including renewed strikes, with Brent still above $115/bbl.
Resumption of Hezbollah-Israel hostilities, which pushed Brent to $117.44/bbl intraday.
An inconclusive Israeli election, with deadlock or a repeat vote possible, and a different approach to the Iran endgame depending on the winner.
Debt financing risk for AI-dependent neocloud companies, as raised by Elon Musk in his post on X.
Large equity issuance, such as Meta's planned $95bn stock sale.
European energy supply, with natural gas at a post-2022 high on a Norway outage.
Political and sovereign risk in France and Brazil.
vol_and_positioning: iTraxx Crossover closed at 333 (-8), iTraxx Europe at 67 (-1), CDX 125 at 63 (-1), iTraxx Senior Financials at 76 (-2) and iTraxx Subordinated Financials at 131 (-5). Credit spreads tightened across the board with the risk-on tone.
DB's 'Investor Positioning and Flows: Taking Stock Of The Tech Unwind' (Oct 23) is listed as a topical publication. No positioning data is given in this note.
geopolitical: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan (the Mecca Defence Alliance) met Iranian representatives in Tehran to promote regional stability. Iran said it would support 'any understanding' that strengthened regional unity.
Last week's reports said the US and Israeli militaries had begun drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran.
Reuters reported that Hezbollah was preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities with Israel.

Israel's election today could produce a Netanyahu-led government, an opposition or unity government, deadlock or another election. Eisenkot favours military intervention if necessary to stop an Iranian nuclear weapon but not regime change, and Netanyahu holds that regime change is necessary.
Tensions with Iran could re-escalate after the US midterms.
Brazil: Lula won the presidential election in a surprise victory over Flávio Bolsonaro, triggering a sharp sell-off in Brazilian assets.
France: weekend protests were controlled, unlike the previous weekend, and Moody's left France's credit rating unchanged on Friday.

tension_points.bull_case: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian representatives in Tehran, and Iran said it would support 'any understanding' that strengthened regional unity. This news dominated and Brent settled 0.78% lower.
tension_points.bear_case: Reports last week said the US and Israeli militaries had begun drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran, and Reuters reported Hezbollah was preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities with Israel. Investors remain wary of extrapolating from diplomatic efforts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Re-escalation after the US midterms, or a resumption of Hezbollah-Israel hostilities, which pushed Brent to $117.44/bbl intraday.

theme_stances.key_argument: The vote will not remove the prospect of another confrontation with Iran, but it could shape what Israel wants any confrontation to achieve.
theme_stances.evidence: So the aftermath and coalition arithmetic will be very relevant well beyond Israel.
